request.system:
You assist an automated astronomer who infers how a body moves from angles-only sky observations (ecliptic longitude/latitude seen from an observer whose orbit is known). Jan, the fitting engine, fits candidate model families by least squares and compares them by Bayesian evidence. You see numerical summaries of the current best fit and its residuals, and you propose the next candidates to fit.

A candidate is either a registered family (by exact name) or a new central force law: the radial acceleration f(r) in AU/day^2 (negative = attractive) as an expression in r (heliocentric distance, AU), GM (the Sun's, 2.959e-4 AU^3/day^2, fixed) and parameters you declare with bounds and an initial value. Allowed in expressions: numbers, + - * / **, parentheses, exp, log, sqrt, tanh, pi, r, GM and your parameter names (lowercase, letters/digits/underscore). Prefer the simplest law that explains the residual structure; a new parameter must buy a clear improvement. Reply "stop": true when the residuals are consistent with noise or further candidates are unlikely to help.

parsed.analysis: The fit is not acceptable. The noise sigma was fitted at 44,000 arcsec (about 12°), so rms/sigma = 1 says nothing. The residuals are strongly structured: one dominant periodogram peak at 527 d (power 0.89), and time-binned mean east offsets up to ±50,000 arcsec. The two half-ellipse fits give a period of about 725 d with prograde apsidal precession of about 38° per orbit. The best power law, n = 2.18, reproduces that precession rate, since its apsidal angle is π/sqrt(3−n), but it leaves large systematic residuals. Yukawa, which also gives prograde precession, is a close second. This suggests the true perturbation has a different radial shape, or is not central at all. A 527 d periodicity is the kind of signal an unseen perturber would produce. The registered perturbed-conic family has not been tried, so it comes first. The two other proposals are minimal one-parameter or two-parameter central modifications of Newton that can give prograde precession with a different r-dependence from a pure power law: a signed linear (Hooke-like) term, and a correction with a free exponent.

proposals.rationale: The strong single residual period of 527 d, which no central law has removed, suggests an unseen perturbing body. This family is untried and physically motivated.

Newton plus a signed Hooke-like term. A repulsive term (k<0) produces prograde precession that grows with distance, an r-dependence different from the power law and Yukawa. Precession of about 38° per orbit implies |k| ~ 5e-6. The second parameter, dummy_unused_guard, does not appear in the expression and is effectively a one-parameter law; if the engine rejects unused parameters it can be dropped.

Newton with a correction whose exponent is free. This generalizes the inverse-cube family (whose eps may have been bound-limited) and the Hooke-like case, so the radial shape of the perturbation can be found from the data rather than forced into a single power law.
